texts.preamble: Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Kabc020333662018 In The Court Of The Iv Addl. Judge And Member, Motor Vehicle Accident Tribunal & Acjm, Bengaluru (Scch-6) Present: Smt. Chetana S.F. B.A., L.L.B., Iv Addl., Judge & Mact & Acjm, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 2nd Day Of July 2025 M.V.C.No.7865 Of 2018 Sampathkumar Nagaraj S/o Nagaraj Aged about 21 years R/a # 332, Seebam Samanapalli village and post Krishnagiri Taluk Tamil Nadu-635 117 Alternative address: Naragund Institutions College Hostel Dhathathreya nagar Hosakerahalli cross 100 feet ring road Bengaluru-560 085 Scch-6 2 Mvc.7865/2018 .. Petitioner - Versus - 1. H.S.Khiser Anjum Major S/o Mr.C.S.Hashim Syed R/at Dr.Alams Estate Shanthi layout, Ramamurthynagar Bengaluru-560 016 (Rc owner of Mgv No.KA-53-C-4047) 2. Mrs.Naveen Azra Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/ 1 Major R/at Dr.Alams Estate Shanthi layout Ramamurthynagar Bengaluru-560 016 (Insured of Mgv No.KA-53-C-4047) 3. Reliance General Insurance co., Ltd., # 28, East wing, 5th floor Centenary building Mg road, Bengaluru-01 Rep by the Manager (Insurer of Mgv No.KA-53-C-4047 Policy No.9904972334001241 validity period 31-3-2017 to 30-3-2018) ..... Respondents (By Sri.R.Chandrashekhar-Advocate for petitioner Sri.C.S.Hashim Saed-Advocate for respondent No.1 and 2 Sri.V.S.Naidu-Advocate for respondent No.3) Scch-6 3 Mvc.7865/2018 Judgment
texts.facts: On 4-11-2017 at about 3.45 a.m. when the petitioner was riding the motor cycle Honda Activa bearing No.KA-53- H-8617 along with his friends Philip Abraham and Mahateja as pillion riders on Timber layout main road, Timber yard layout, Bengaluru, near Rose wood international hotel, driver of the MGV bearing No.KA-53-C-4047 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, on extreme right side of the road and dashed against the motor cycle. Due to impact, petitioner and pillion riders sustained severe injuries and motor cycle was also damaged. Immediately petitioner was sifted to hospital, after first aid treatment shifted to Fortis hospital, thereafter shifted to St.John's medical college hospital, Bengaluru wherein took treatment as inpatient and discharged on 12-12-2017. The petitioner spent amount of Rs.10 lakhs for hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and other incidental expenses. Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.50 lakhs from the respondents. 3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 to 3 appeared through their respective counsel and only respondent No.1 and 3 filed their respective written statement. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement contended that the driver of the lorry was very careful and had taken all precautions and it is negligence of the petitioner who was driving without observing the lorry was already was in the road by taking the right turn and petitioner who was on the wheels the accident was caused only due to the carelessness and negligent and not keeping presence of mind by the petitioner who was driving negligently driven and due to this reason the accident occurred. Hence prays to dismiss the petition. 5. The respondent No.3 in its written statement contended that the above petition is bad for non joinder of necessary and proper parties as the petitioner has failed to implead the owner and insured of the Honda Activa bearing reg.No.KA-53-H-8617. The owner of the Honda Aciva intentionally entrusted/allowed 3 adult persons to travel on the honda activa on the road knowing fully well that the seating capacity of the honda activa is only 2, in the complaint, FIR, charge sheet and other police documents clearly reflects that at the time of accident there were three members were traveling on the honda activa. This respondent is not necessary and proper party for the adjudication fo the above case. The jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the rider and owner of the honda activa bearing No.KA-53-H-8617. Since there was no valid insurance policy to the honda activa, the jurisdictional police colluded with the petitioner has filed false charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle as A1 only with an intention to claim compensation by taking advantage of policy of insurance. This respondent seeks protection u/s 147 & 149 of MV Act. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive. The claim is bad for non compliance of section 158(6) and 134(c) of MV Act. 7. The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined two witnesses as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked Exs.P1 to P137 documents. The respondent No.3 got examined its Assistant Manager as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1 and 2. 8. My answers to the above issues are as follows:- Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:- REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:- In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked Ex-P1 to 137 documents i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, statement, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, col. 133 notice, reply, discharge summaries, medical bills, prescriptions, 3 photos, CD, aadhaar card.
texts.arguments: 11. On the other hand, counsel for the respondent No.3 has seriously disputed the cause and manner of the accident and contended that the accident has been taken place due to the sole rash and negligent driving of the motor cycle Honda Activa by the petitioner himself who was riding along with the two pillion riders. It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that the petitioner was riding the Honda Activa bearing No.KA-53-H-8617 without coverage of the insurance policy and without driving licence and along with the two pillion riders in a rash and negligent manner with high speed early in the morning at 3.45 a.m. and lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the rare right wheel portion of the goods vehicle MGV bearing No.KA-53-C-4047 and fell down and sustained injuries. Further it was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that the complainant eyewitness has voluntarily lodge the complaint before the police authorities stating that accident has been occurred solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Activa honda who rode the same along with the two pillion riders and dashed against the rare right wheel of the goods vehicle. Further argued that even the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the rider and owner of the Activa honda for offence punishable u/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC 128 r/w 177, 3(1) r/w 181, 146 r/w 196 of IMV Act by contending that accused No.2 rider of the motor cycle Activa honda riding the same along with two pillion riders without coverage of the insurance policy and without valid and effective driving licence and thereby caused the accident. Further argued that since the petitioner was driving the vehicle which was not having the valid insurance policy, the petitioner colluding with the jurisdictional police and made the police to file false charge sheet against the driver of the goods vehicle as accused No.1 only with intention to claim the compensation from the respondents. Further argued that respondent is not at all responsible for the cause of the accident. Hence above claim petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent. 13. In this regard-The Hon'ble Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.79/2020 (Mohammed Siddiqui & Anr., v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., & Ors.), has held thus: Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/ 4 The fact that the deceased was riding on a motor cycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence. Section 128 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, imposes a restriction on the driver of a two wheeled motor cycle, not to carry more than one person on the motor cycle. Section 194C inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers and pillion riders. Though counsel for the respondent No.3 contended that police colluding with the petitioner has filed the charge sheet against the driver of the lorry, but no materials and evidence are placed on record to prove that the charge sheet filed by the police is wrong, defective and collusive. In fact, the proof of accident itself is sufficient for the purpose of this case, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2001 ACJ 1975 (Sri. Kumaresh V/s. The Divisional Manager, National Insurance Com. Ltd., and another) , it was held in the above decision that, in the motor accident case strict proof of rash and negligent driving need not be established, as was required in criminal cases. Sampath Kumar Nagaraj vs H.S. Khiser Anjum on 2 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85442266/ 6 18. RW-1 pleaded his ignorance for the suggestion that driver of the lorry has pleaded guilty for offence charged against him and paid the fine. If at all there was no rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, certainly driver of the lorry would have contesting the case and would not have pleaded guilty. 19. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter. 21. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
